There's this saying when you're starting a farm or homestead, to not get any more than two new species of critters per year so that you can focus well enough on them to make sure their needs are met.

I honored this with chickens and goats this year. (As an aside I'm fully responsible for them, husband helps when i need him to but he is mostly assisting me when I need it, he chose bees and I also suit up to assist him but I know little about them). However, my well intentioned mother in law bought the kids rabbits for Easter.

Me, scrambling to figure out their needs, read up and figured, ok, I've got this! They're rabbits, easy peasy, right? Everytime I've been to someone's house who had rabbits they were in awful, tiny cages without food or water. Ours were living like Kings already by contrast. They're going to be fine.

Well, last night was the first night our local bobcat paid us a visit since February when my husband almost had his pelt. We have baby goats that can squeeze between 4"x4" wire and we had to do some moving of critters, babies in with the chickens in the 12'x12' coop, put the bunnies in their cage in there too since we worried about the bobcat being able to break their cage, coop is in the center of the main goat paddock (300'x100')and we put our bullies in there to guard (American bullies. They're not pit bulls). They've been great guardians during the day while releasing the herd and they did just as well in the night.

Once coyotes came, they scared them off. Bobcat came, same. It was a long night because I woke at each encounter and sat at the window with my scope hoping to sight them. Drawback to a paddock in the woods, you can't see shit.

I'm relieved when the sun starts coming up and the normal bustle starts. Those critters will attack during the day but very unlikely. I finally get a couple hours of sleep. Then get up to do morning chores.

I find three dead bunny rabbits. No wounds. Laying still within the cage. They apparently died of heart attack. In all the reading I had done, which was really less than 1-2 hour's worth, no one mentioned these bastards keel over from even an excited toddler being rambunctious (we have one of those... Some days I think there's a gnome secretly feeding him caffeine laced candies when I'm not looking...). The consideration that the dogs barking to keep the predators at bay would kill them never entered my mind.

I feel bad. The kids are pretty sad about it. My daughter had read up on them more than I had and she never came across this information, we primarily had been focused on avoiding sickness from any elimination from any of the animals, what they needed to eat for optimal health, what foods were poison, and best living quarters.

Anyway. Heed the warning. Only two new livestock per year per responsible party. It's a sad waste of life and I really hope it was a fast death. I always wondered why there wasn't an overabundance of rabbits considering they have up to 14 kits at a time... Now I know why.

I have lost so many chickens, rabbits, cats...

You get used to it, just soldier on. Good lesson for the kids, too.
